lines: Find the verbs first: they tell you what happens.
اِبْحَثْ أَوَّلًا عَنِ الْأَفْعَالِ، فَهِيَ تَقُولُ مَاذَا حَدَثَ.
Next to each verb find who did it (ـُ) and what it was done to (ـَ).
بَعْدَ كُلِّ فِعْلٍ اِبْحَثْ عَنِ الْفَاعِلِ (ـُ) وَعَنِ الْمَفْعُولِ (ـَ).
Joiners (وَ فَ ثُمَّ) tell you the order of events.
الْحُرُوفُ وَ فَ ثُمَّ تُرَتِّبُ الْأَحْدَاثَ.

slides.head_en: Story: Friday morning in the market (1)
lines: فِي صَبَاحِ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى السُّوقِ.
On Friday morning Ahmad went with his father to the market.
There were many people in the market.
The father bought bread and milk for the guests.
ثُمَّ نَظَرَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى مُصْحَفٍ جَدِيدٍ.
Then Ahmad looked at a new muṣḥaf.

slides.head_en: Story: Friday morning in the market (2)
lines: So the father bought the muṣḥaf and gave it to Ahmad.
ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
Then Ahmad went with his father to the mosque.
And Ahmad prayed with his father.
And Ahmad prayed (made duʿāʾ) for his father.

slides.note: Verb first, then the one doing it, then what it was done to.
slides.note_ar: الْفِعْلُ أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ الْفَاعِلُ، ثُمَّ مَا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ.

cards.def_en: the noun in ـُ after the verb
look for لِأَنَّ or the result

sents: And Ahmad prayed with his father.

إِلَى أَيْنَ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ؟
to the market (and then to the mosque)

slides.big_en: 1 verb · 2 who · 3 what / where · 4 next line
slides.small: Do not translate word by word: find the verb, the doer and the thing acted on, then say the whole sentence.
slides.small_ar: اِبْحَثْ عَنِ الْفِعْلِ وَالْفَاعِلِ وَالْمَفْعُولِ، ثُمَّ قُلِ الْجُمْلَةَ كُلَّهَا. لَا تُتَرْجِمْ كَلِمَةً كَلِمَةً.

slides.why: A reader says: “The book saw the boy.” Wrong! الْوَلَدُ ends in ـُ (the one doing), الْكِتَابَ ends in ـَ (the thing seen). The boy saw the book.
slides.why_ar: قَارِئٌ يَقُولُ: «رَأَى الْكِتَابُ الْوَلَدَ». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! الْوَلَدُ فَاعِلٌ (ـُ) وَالْكِتَابَ مَفْعُولٌ (ـَ). الْوَلَدُ رَأَى الْكِتَابَ.

can: I can read a short story and say who did what, to whom, and where.
I can use the verb, the doer (ـُ) and the thing acted on (ـَ) to follow a text.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ قِصَّةً قَصِيرَةً وَأَقُولَ مَنْ فَعَلَ مَاذَا وَأَيْنَ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْتَعْمِلَ الْفِعْلَ وَالْفَاعِلَ (ـُ) وَالْمَفْعُولَ (ـَ) لِأَفْهَمَ النَّصَّ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Read the story of the Friday market, then answer.
lines: جَاءَ سَالِمُ إِلَى السُّوقِ فِي صَبَاحِ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ.
On Friday morning Salim came to the market.
كَانَ السُّوقُ كَبِيرًا، وَكَانَ فِيهِ نَاسٌ كَثِيرُونَ.
The market was big, and there were many people in it.
رَأَى سَالِمُ صَدِيقَهُ عُمَرَ عِنْدَ بَابِ السُّوقِ.
Salim saw his friend Umar at the door of the market.
Umar said: “My father bought bread for the guests.”
قَالَ سَالِمُ: «هَلِ الْمَسْجِدُ قَرِيبٌ مِنَ السُّوقِ؟»
Salim said: “Is the mosque near the market?”
قَالَ عُمَرُ: «نَعَمْ، هُوَ قَرِيبٌ، وَالْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْآنَ.»
Umar said: “Yes, it is near, and the Habib is in the mosque now.”
So Salim and Umar went to the mosque.
وَصَلَّى سَالِمُ مَعَ عُمَرَ ثُمَّ دَعَا لِأَبِيهِ.
And Salim prayed with Umar, then he prayed for his father.

lines: Yusuf came to the Habib’s ribāṭ.

Yusuf thanked Umar and went back to his house.

ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
